title: Rigoberta Menchú's birth chart
metaDescription: Rigoberta Menchú's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.7° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Mars sit 0.3° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads identity and drive as a single working part. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 18.7° Capricorn, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Venus. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: the Sun to Mars, a trine with 0.3° of slack. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Mercury conjunction Saturn at 1.8°, and Neptune sextile Pluto at 2.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Sagittarius at 28.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Taurus at 19.1° is in detriment; Saturn in Capricorn at 0.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The balance sheet: earth 5, fire 2, water 2, air 1 across the elements, and fixed 5, cardinal 3, mutable 2 across the modalities. An earth emphasis reads as trust in the tangible: the plan matters less than whether the thing stands up. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Capricorn into Aquarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.9° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
